query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

generation.hypothesis: Grain-boundary segregation and precipitation of brittle phases in high-entropy alloys, triggered by high-temperature exposure and subsequent cooling, lead to toughness degradation due to the formation of brittle grain-boundary films.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase high-entropy alloy with a compositionally complex structure
generation.intervention: High-temperature exposure (800°C for 100 hours) followed by cooling to room temperature
generation.conditions: Vacuum environment to minimize oxidation and contamination
generation.structural_mediator: Grain-boundary segregation and precipitation of brittle phases
generation.mechanism: Thermally-activated diffusion of solute atoms to grain boundaries, leading to the formation of brittle grain-boundary films
generation.predicted_outcome: 30% reduction in toughness (measured by Charpy impact test) compared to the initial baseline
generation.baseline: Initial toughness of the single-phase high-entropy alloy (20 J/cm²)
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 25°C to 800°C, loading rate: 10⁻³ s⁻¹ to 10³ s⁻¹
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and processing history of the high-entropy alloy may influence the grain-boundary segregation and precipitation behavior, potentially affecting the toughness degradation

falsification_experiment.design: Combined experiment and simulation approach, using in situ characterization (e.g., TEM, APT) and atomistic simulations (e.g., MD, DFT) to study grain boundary evolution and toughness degradation
measurements: Grain-boundary segregation and precipitation, toughness (Charpy impact test), microstructure (TEM, SEM)
Grain-boundary film thickness and composition (APT, EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the toughness degradation is less than 10% (i.e., 2 J/cm²) after high-temperature exposure and cooling, the hypothesis is falsified, indicating that grain-boundary segregation and precipitation are not the primary mechanisms governing toughness degradation in this high-entropy alloy
